findings.issue_text: Hostnames are compared case-sensitively even though DNS names are case-insensitive, causing URLs such as `https://EXAMPLE.com/user` on an `example.com` instance to render only `EXAMPLE.com` instead of the complete path.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hostnames are compared case-sensitively even though DNS names are case-insensitive, causing URLs such as `https://EXAMPLE.com/user` on an `example.com` instance to render only `EXAMPLE.com` instead of the complete path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. In the `website_name` method in `user_serializer.rb`, the code compares hostnames using `==` and `ends_with?` which are case-sensitive string operations. For example, `website_host == discourse_host` would fail if one is 'EXAMPLE.com' and the other is 'example.com'. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive per RFC, so 'EXAMPLE.com' should match 'example.com'. The code should use `casecmp` or downcase both strings before comparison. This would cause the method to return just the hostname instead of hostname+path for URLs with different casing.
